title: Company-Delay Goodwill on Late Balance Charges
content:
# Company-Delay Goodwill on Late Balance Charges

Window Replacement Contracts. When Ridgeline delayed the project, goodwill days are added before late periods are counted, read from the contract's Installation Jobs and Factory Production Orders records.

**Rule.** The company-delay goodwill is 14 days (the both-delays goodwill days) when the contract's installation job carries a company-initiated reschedule and its factory order shipped after its committed ship date, 7 days (the one-delay goodwill days) when only one of those two happened, and no goodwill days when neither did. The goodwill days are calendar days added to the date from which full 30-day late periods are counted (the late-charge start date).

**Records read.** The installation job is the contract's job that is not cancelled, and a reschedule counts when it is logged on that job as initiated by the company. The factory order is the contract's order that is not cancelled; it shipped late when its ship date is after its committed ship date. There is no factory delay when there is no order or the order has not shipped, and no installation reschedule when there is no job.

| Company-initiated installation reschedule | Factory order shipped after committed ship date | Goodwill days |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 14 |
| Yes | No | 7 |
| No | Yes | 7 |
| No | No | 0 |

## Hypothetical readings

- A job with one reschedule initiated by the customer and none by the company, and an order shipped on its committed date: 0 days.
- A job rescheduled once by the company, and an order committed for 2031-05-02 that shipped 2031-05-09: 14 days.
